filesChanged: .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh: the rule inverted — the gate judges the tool a command reaches, approving only the word immediately after scripts/repo-tool.sh and the pinned node_modules/.bin path; comments stripped before judging; whole-basename, case-sensitive matching; one report per segment; the package-manager branch given four cases with the last refusing rather than swallowing; the package-runner rule kept, since it still catches a `bunx vite` the tool rule does not. The header's numbered rules rewritten to match.

.github/scripts/check-check-commands.test.sh: additions only (the diff removes no line) — the four lines from this repository's own guides as must-keep-passing fixtures, the YAML-block pair, the pinned-path spellings, the prefixed and nested runners, the manager subcommands in all four cases, and an unknown subcommand both ways.
trickyParts: The approved form has to be judged at the tool, not at the segment's first word: a fenced YAML block in docs/solutions holds `run: ../../scripts/repo-tool.sh biome check --error-on-warnings src/`, whose segment starts with `run:`. The rule is therefore 'the word immediately before the tool is the wrapper', which reads the same in a shell line, a recipe and a YAML scalar.

A naive 'the segment contains a tool's name' refuses three lines already in this repository's guides, which I measured with a probe before writing the rule: two trailing comments and one YAML block. Comment stripping and whole-basename matching are what make the inversion usable, and both are pinned by fixtures rather than by the tree.
`exec` is not reachable in this agent's own shell, so the tester's `exec bunx` spelling has to be measured through /bin/sh.
deviations: The package-runner rule survives the inversion although the tool rule subsumes it for every check tool: a prescribed `bunx vite` is still the registry resolution this issue is about, and its cases are already in the suite. The boundary is deliberate and stated in the header — a runner behind a prefix that names something other than a check tool (`exec bunx vite`) is not reported, because AC2 is about the commands for lint, types and tests.
openQuestions: Unchanged: AC3's full line, AC4's daemon half and AC5's two-role form are production-check criteria and need the worker image pin and the one `runtime.kubernetes.setup` line, which must name none of the runtime-owned variables.
No Makefile, justfile or Taskfile exists in this repository (checked), so no prescribed command hides in one; if one is ever added it is a context this gate does not judge.
discoveredComplexity: Two rounds of failures came from the same shape: a gate that reads the command word is a denylist of spellings, and the spellings are unbounded. Judging the tool is the only formulation where the question 'can this line reach the squat?' has a bounded answer.

The first draft of the inversion still carried a first-word special case for package managers, and it let `pnpm exec biome` and `yarn biome` through; my own battery caught it before the work was accepted. An allowlist of ordinary subcommands with a refusal for anything else is what closes it.
